newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan reminds Clinton of peace initiative vow.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan reminds Clinton of peace initiative vow.

text.p: Pakistan on Thursday greeted the re-election of U.S. President Bill Clinton and said it hoped he would take a promised initiative to settle political problems in South Asia.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman said Islamabad had also "noted with satisfaction" that several U.S. Congressmen friendly to Pakistan had also been re-elected, and Senator Larry Pressler, considered hostile to Pakistan, had lost the re-election bid.
Pressler had authored legislation that led to a cutoff of U.S. military aid to Pakistan.

The spokesman recalled Clinton had said in a campaign statement that he would take an initiative towards settling political problems in South Asia, where arch-foes India and Pakistan have a longstanding dispute over the Himalayan region of Kashmir.
"We will look forward to such an initiative by the new administration of the United States," the spokesman said.
Washington has offered to mediate between India and Pakistan over Kashmir if both countries agreed, a suggestion welcomed by Islamabad but firmly rejected by India.

Pakistan's official comment appeared tepid compared to that of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, who on Wednesday enthusiasatically greeted Clinton's re-election saying he was "the perfect person" to lead the United States into the 21st century.

President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto's three-year-old government on Tuesday, dissolved the National Assembly and named a caretaker prime minister to supervise parliamentary elections set for February 3.

The anti-Bhutto Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party made no comment on Clinton's win, but welcomed the defeat of Pressler, widely disparaged in Pakistan for sponsoring a legislative amendment that halted U.S. military aid to Islamabad.
A statement by PML information secretary Mushahid Hussain said Pressler's defeat by Senator Tim Johnson on Tuesday "should augur well for Pakistan".
He urged the Pakistani government to take vigorous steps to have the Pressler Amendment repealed because, he said, after Pressler's defeat the law stood discredited.
Pakistan, a threshold nuclear power, has refused to sign the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty or the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty unless arch-foe India does the same.
